description: A machine-readable code explaining why the row results of a query against an aggregate-only source were withheld. When such a query requests row results, it is rejected with this code rather than returning rows.
name: RowSuppressionReasonCode

enum.name: NO_QUASI_IDENTIFIERS
enum.description: The aggregate-only source defines no quasi-identifier columns, so it never returns row-level results; any query that requests rows is rejected.

enum.name: QID_PROJECTED
enum.description: A quasi-identifier column is projected in the select list as more than the argument of a COUNT (e.g. selected directly or via 'select *').

enum.name: QID_IN_NON_COUNT_AGGREGATE
enum.description: A quasi-identifier column is used as the argument of an aggregate function other than COUNT (e.g. MAX, MIN, SUM, AVG, GROUP_CONCAT), or any column or value is used as the argument of an aggregate function whose result depends on the number of rows in a group (any aggregate other than COUNT, MIN, MAX, and AVG, e.g. SUM, GROUP_CONCAT, JSON_ARRAYAGG).

enum.name: QID_IN_GROUP_BY
enum.description: A quasi-identifier column appears in a GROUP BY clause.

enum.name: QID_IN_ORDER_BY
enum.description: A quasi-identifier column, or any COUNT, appears in an ORDER BY clause.

enum.name: QID_IN_SELECT_DISTINCT
enum.description: A quasi-identifier column appears in a SELECT DISTINCT clause.

enum.name: QID_IN_EXPRESSION
enum.description: A quasi-identifier column, or any COUNT, is used within an arithmetic or string expression rather than as the whole value of its select-list column.

enum.name: QID_AGGREGATE_IN_FILTER
enum.description: A column whose value is an aggregate of a quasi-identifier (e.g. a COUNT computed by a MaterializedView or VirtualTable) is used to filter the rows, whether in a WHERE clause, an additional filter, a selected facet, or a cohort filter. Filtering on such a value would identify the rows whose count is below the suppression threshold.

enum.name: AGGREGATE_NOT_PERMITTED
enum.description: The defining SQL of a VirtualTable read by the query uses an aggregate in a shape that is not permitted for an aggregate-only source. Each aggregate must be the whole value of a select-list column, and must be either a COUNT or COUNT(DISTINCT ...), or a list of the distinct values of one column that is not a quasi-identifier: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT e [ORDER BY col] [SEPARATOR 'literal']), where e reads only that column through CONCAT or REPLACE with string literals, optionally wrapped in CONCAT with string literals and a CAST to a column model.
